framing: Assume attacker has acquired a valid `auth:sanctum` token of a low-privilege role (POS Operator, Chef, Customer, stale staff). Token holds the X-Api-Key shared secret (extracted from admin SPA bundle or env leak). Attacker enumerates /admin/* endpoints.

attack_surface_size.attack_radius_if_one_gate_missing: Single endpoint scope unless cross-tenant via BranchScope bypass

attack_scenarios.attacker_role: Any sanctum-authenticated user (POS Operator, Chef, even revoked-but-not-revoked stale token)
attack_scenarios.preconditions: Attacker knows or enumerates {user_id, order_id} pair belonging to a victim
attack_scenarios.exploit: MyOrderDetailsController has zero middleware. OrderService::orderDetails (L1411-1422) checks `$order->user_id == $user->id` — BOTH come from URL params, NOT from auth(). Caller-identity check missing.
attack_scenarios.blast_radius: Same-branch staff: any customer order in their branch. Admin token: cross-branch (BranchScope auto-bypassed for Admin role). Discloses: transaction (payment refs, last4), orderItems, branch, user.
attack_scenarios.mitigation_existing: BranchScope on Order limits to same-branch for non-Admin. Attacker still gets any same-branch customer.
attack_scenarios.mitigation_proposed_REVISED: Endpoint is consumed by 3 admin SPA views (Customer/Waiter/DeliveryBoy detail) AND NO frontend account view. Naive `auth()->id() === $user->id` BREAKS the 3 admin flows. Correct fix: `$this->middleware('permission:customers_show|waiters_show|delivery-boys_show')` (Spatie OR) in MyOrderDetailsController constructor. Cleaner V1.0.2: split into 3 dedicated endpoints each with its own perm.
attack_scenarios.verdict: P0 documented — NOT healed in Round 1 (multi-consumer perm-alternation requires sentinel test before commit). V1.0.2 redesign target.

attack_scenarios.scenario: Tracking pixel injection / cross-site script via Analytic.body
attack_scenarios.path: POST /api/admin/setting/analytic — gated; GET /api/admin/setting/analytic — UNGATED for index/show
attack_scenarios.exploit: AnalyticController::store/update/destroy are gated (S-3 in Security report) but `index` and `show` are NOT. Attacker can ENUMERATE existing analytic integrations (GTM IDs, FB pixel IDs, custom HTML snippets) of any tenant.
attack_scenarios.blast_radius: Disclosure of tracking-pixel config. Possibly contains 3rd-party API keys if devs misuse the body field.

attack_scenarios.preconditions: Attacker token + key + MenuTemplateController truly ungated
attack_scenarios.exploit: MenuTemplateController has no permission middleware (S-2). Need to verify whether route group wraps it. If ungated → any token holder could create/destroy menu templates, breaking catalog UX for staff using templates.
attack_scenarios.blast_radius: Catalog UX availability for menu builder. Not a tenant-data leak per se, but a denial-of-service / mischief vector.

attack_scenarios.scenario: Privilege escalation via Administrator creation at branch_id=0
attack_scenarios.attacker_role: Branch Manager (has administrators_create perm? — uncertain) or any staff with administrators_create
attack_scenarios.verdict: MITIGATED — AdministratorRequest withValidator after-rule (L74-91) blocks non-Admin/non-Tenant Admin callers from setting branch_id=0. Heal commit visible. Defense verified.

attack_scenarios.scenario: Role permission matrix enumeration without settings perm
attack_scenarios.attacker_role: POS Operator or stale Customer token
attack_scenarios.verdict: MITIGATED — PermissionController::__construct gates all methods (incl. index) via `$this->middleware(['permission:settings'])` per M-R3-P0-A heal. Sentinel test exists (PermissionControllerIndexAuthzTest).

attack_scenarios.scenario: Shared API key extraction → DoS via throttle bucket exhaustion
attack_scenarios.attacker_role: Any party with X-Api-Key (extractable from SPA bundle if not env-loaded; extractable from server env if filesystem read)
attack_scenarios.exploit: X-Api-Key is a shared deployment secret. If leaked, attacker can hit endpoints up to throttle limit and exhaust per-IP bucket. Cannot mutate without sanctum token though.
attack_scenarios.verdict: P2 — defense-in-depth. Real fix is OAuth/PKCE not shared-secret-header. V1.0.2 backlog. Per-IP throttle already mitigates blast radius (TrustProxies fix Wave 3 P1).

attack_scenarios.scenario: DefaultAccess privilege bypass via branch_id forgery
attack_scenarios.exploit: If staff submits branch_id=0 hoping to switch their default branch to Admin scope.
attack_scenarios.mitigation_existing: DefaultAccessService::storeOrUpdate L48-51 coerces branch_id back to caller's branch if not Admin. Defense in place.

attack_scenarios.scenario: PaymentGateway secret read via show endpoint
attack_scenarios.exploit: PaymentGatewayController is gated `permission:settings`. But Stripe secret_key in response body? Depends on PaymentGatewayResource — need to verify it doesn't leak credentials.
attack_scenarios.verdict: Defer — not deeply audited in 1500-word cap. Logged as V1.0.1 task.

attack_scenarios.scenario: Audit trail tampering via direct ActionLog mutation
attack_scenarios.path: No endpoint — but is there a `ActionLog::create()` from user-controlled input?
attack_scenarios.exploit: DashboardService::auditTrail reads ActionLog. Writes happen via observers/events. Need to verify no user-controlled `details` field allows XSS when displayed in admin UI.
attack_scenarios.verdict: Defer — would need Vue rendering check of admin/dashboard/AuditTrailComponent.vue. P2.

summary_attack_surface.P0_chain_to_total_compromise: No — R-1 IDOR is bounded by BranchScope for non-Admin. Compromise of Admin token → game over (as expected). No path from low-priv token to Admin escalation observed.

most_dangerous_path_if_chained: R-1 + branch-X staff token → enumerate every customer/order in branch X → exfiltrate transaction payment refs, customer PII (name, addresses via .with('user'))
verdict: 1 NEW P0 (R-1 / S-1 IDOR — same finding). 2 P1 heal-eligible (R-2, R-3). 2 P1 confirmed mitigated by recent heals. 4 P2 deferred to V1.0.1/V1.0.2 backlog. Admin gating posture is generally tight (71/87 = 82% explicit gate) BUT the gaps that exist are not benign — 1 of 16 ungated controllers is the IDOR vector.
